name: Guy Levy
current_role: Founder, Managing Partner & CIO, Soleus Capital Management (Greenwich, CT)
profile: Guy Levy founded and runs Soleus Capital, a Greenwich-based healthcare-focused hedge fund and private equity investor. Through Soleus he is a 10%+ holder of EDAP TMS (focal ultrasound) and Parabilis Medicines, where Soleus bought about $10M of stock around the June 2026 IPO. Soleus reported roughly $2B in discretionary assets in 2024.
interesting_fact: Before launching Soleus he worked at Paulson & Co., Shumway Capital, Warburg Pincus and Morgan Stanley; he holds a B.A. from Yale.
notes: Low public profile; career details come from aggregator profiles (Insider Monkey, Marketscreener). No published press contact for Soleus found. Route is via Soleus Capital in Greenwich. Healthcare/biotech investor, not an energy fit.

name: Charles L. Treadway
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Vistance Networks (formerly CommScope); stepping down Feb 1, 2027; Director, AZZ Inc.
profile: Chuck Treadway has been CEO of CommScope (renamed Vistance Networks in Jan 2026) since October 2020. He led the sale of several divisions, including RUCKUS to Belden, leaving Vistance focused on Aurora Networks. Before that he was CEO of Accudyne Industries (2016-20) and Thomas & Betts (2012-16). He plans to step down on Feb 1, 2027.
interesting_fact: He has run businesses in the U.S., Mexico, Europe and Asia, including as CEO of a Schneider-Swire joint venture in China and president of Grupo Tesa Mexico (Yale Security).
deep_cut_fact: He started as an engineer at Square D. At the University of Louisiana at Lafayette (B.S.E.E. 1988) he was student government president for the College of Engineering and president of the Louisiana Engineering Society. He later earned an M.S.E.E. from Clemson and an MBA from Harvard.
notes: CEO departure announced (effective Feb 1, 2027), so he may soon be free to talk about the CommScope breakup. Some newer releases list Weiwei Tan as the media contact.

name: Paul Elliot Mann
current_role: Executive Chairman & CEO, ASP Isotopes Inc. (returned as CEO Jan 2026); Chairman, Quantum Leap Energy (planned nuclear-fuel spin-out)
profile: Paul E. Mann co-founded ASP Isotopes in 2021. The company enriches isotopes in Pretoria, South Africa, and is developing HALEU nuclear fuel through Quantum Leap Energy, a unit it plans to spin out. Before ASPI he was CFO of PolarityTE and a healthcare and chemicals investor at Soros Fund Management, Highbridge and DSAM, after 11 years as a sell-side analyst at Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank.
interesting_fact: He has pitched enriched carbon-14 at about $24,000 per gram, which he said is more than 400 times the price of gold. He got involved when ASPI's South African scientists were running out of money while building their enrichment plant.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a research scientist at Procter & Gamble and is named as the inventor of numerous skin creams in the Oil of Olay range. At Morgan Stanley he was corporate broker to over half of the UK's pharmaceutical companies.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (nuclear fuel/HALEU, isotopes); he often does investor interviews. Took a medical leave Oct 2025 to Jan 2026, so avoid health topics. The IR contact is Jason Assad; some releases list Jacob Rowe instead.

name: Teresa Parker
current_role: President, Asset Servicing, Northern Trust (since Oct 1, 2024)
profile: Teresa Parker has spent her whole career, close to 40 years, at Northern Trust. She has worked in Chicago, Singapore and London, including as head of APAC, global head of securities lending, COO of Asset Servicing and President of EMEA. In 2024 she put off a planned retirement to become President of Asset Servicing, the firm's global custody and fund-administration business for institutional clients.
interesting_fact: She helped build Northern Trust's global custody platform in the 1990s. Financial News named her to its 100 Most Influential Women in Finance list several times, and she is a prominent advocate of flexible working.
deep_cut_fact: Global Custodian inducted her into its 'GC Legends' in 2022. She recalls that the early custody business was so manual that fax instructions slipping behind the machine got lost, and the fix was to 'put a bin bag around the fax machine.'
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder, so not a strong fit for an entrepreneurship podcast. Go through Northern Trust media relations.

name: Randall James Levitt
current_role: President, Nellis Corporation (Potomac, MD); Director, Capital Bancorp Inc. (CBNK)
profile: Randall J. Levitt has been president since 1996 of Nellis Corporation, a private capital management firm in the Maryland suburbs of Washington, DC. Nellis manages a national commercial real estate portfolio and provides wealth advisory services. He has been on the board of Capital Bank since 2004 and of its holding company, Capital Bancorp, since 2012, where he chairs the bank's Special Asset Committee.
interesting_fact: He is a lawyer by training: B.A. summa cum laude from Brandeis and J.D. from Yale Law School.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trustee of the United Jewish Endowment Fund of Greater Washington and sits on its Investment Committee.
notes: Very low public profile; private real-estate investor. No published contact for him or Nellis was found. The only formal route is the Capital Bancorp corporate secretary. Weak fit for the podcast.
